bugs.summary: file.copy(copy.date = TRUE) opens files for exclusive access on Windows: concurrent copies fail, file time not copied if source is open
bugs.creator: kevinushey

comments.creator: kevinushey
comments.text:
On Windows, when file.copy() copies into an existing directory with
copy.date = TRUE, each file is briefly opened for exclusive access in order
to copy its modification time. This has two consequences:

1. If two R processes copy the same files at the same time, one of them can
   fail with a warning of the form "problem copying <from> to <to>:
   Permission denied", and the file is not copied.

2. If the source file is open elsewhere (even just for reading), the file
   time is silently not copied, although file.copy() returns TRUE.

The first case is intermittent, but not rare in practice: it was found via
failures in the renv test suite on GitHub Actions, where two parallel test
workers copy the same directory of files during startup.

Reproducible example:

Both examples were run with R 4.6.1 on Windows Server 2022 (x86_64). The
relevant code is unchanged in trunk (r90591).

(a) The file time is not copied if the source file is open:

    src <- tempfile("source")
    dir <- tempfile("target")
    writeLines("hello", src)
    dir.create(dir)
    Sys.setFileTime(src, as.POSIXct("2020-01-01 12:00:00", tz = "UTC"))

    con <- file(src, "rb")
    file.copy(src, dir, copy.date = TRUE)
    ## [1] TRUE
    close(con)

    file.mtime(src)
    ## [1] "2020-01-01 12:00:00 UTC"
    file.mtime(file.path(dir, basename(src)))
    ## [1] "2026-09-29 03:33:28 UTC"

Expected: the two modification times are the same, as they are if the
connection is not open.

(b) Concurrent copies of the same directory fail:

    copy_repeatedly <- function(source, dates, n) {
      messages <- character()
      for (i in seq_len(n)) {
        target <- tempfile("copy-")
        dir.create(target)
        withCallingHandlers(
          file.copy(source, target, recursive = TRUE, copy.date = dates),
          warning = function(w) {
            messages <<- c(messages, conditionMessage(w))
            invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
          }
        )
        unlink(target, recursive = TRUE)
      }
      messages
    }

    source <- tempfile("source-")
    dir.create(source)
    for (i in 1:100)
      writeLines("hello", file.path(source, sprintf("file-%03i.txt", i)))

    cl <- parallel::makeCluster(4L)

    ## number of warnings in each worker, with copy.date = TRUE
    lengths(parallel::clusterCall(cl, copy_repeatedly, source, TRUE, 100L))
    ## [1] 12 18 10 16

    ## number of warnings in each worker, with copy.date = FALSE
    lengths(parallel::clusterCall(cl, copy_repeatedly, source, FALSE, 100L))
    ## [1] 0 0 0 0

    parallel::stopCluster(cl)

Expected: no warnings in either case. The counts vary from run to run. Each
warning has the form

    problem copying C:\...\source-15a860ad5d4d\file-093.txt to
    C:\...\copy-b8c5beb16b1\source-15a860ad5d4d\file-093.txt:
    Permission denied

Analysis:

When 'to' is a single existing directory, file.copy() calls the internal
do_filecopy(), and on Windows do_copy() calls copyFileTime() for each file
and directory copied (src/main/platform.c). copyFileTime() opens the source
file with

    hFrom = CreateFileW(from, GENERIC_READ, 0, NULL, OPEN_EXISTING,
                        FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS, NULL);

and the destination file in the same way, with GENERIC_WRITE. The share mode
of 0 requests exclusive access. While such a handle is open, attempts to
open the same file elsewhere fail with a sharing violation, so that
_wfopen(this, L"rb") in do_copy() fails in another process, with errno set
to EACCES: this is case 1. above. Conversely, if the file is already open
elsewhere, the CreateFileW() call itself fails, and copyFileTime() returns
without copying the file time: this is case 2. above.

Copying to a file name (rather than into a directory) is not affected, as
then file.copy() uses file.info() and Sys.setFileTime() instead.

Exclusive access is not needed to read or set a file time. file.info()
(also in src/main/platform.c) already opens files to read their times with
a desired access of 0 and with FILE_SHARE_DELETE | FILE_SHARE_READ |
FILE_SHARE_WRITE. For comparison, the equivalent code in Python
(os.utime()), Go (syscall.UtimesNano()), libuv, Rust (std::fs::set_times())
and .NET all request only FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES access when setting file
times.

Proposed patch: attached as file-copy-date-sharing.diff, against trunk
r90591. It changes copyFileTime() to request only FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES (for
the source) and FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES (for the destination), and to allow
sharing as file.info() does. It also adds example (a) to tests/reg-win.R as
a regression test.

The patch is also submitted as https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/pull/345,
where CI results can be seen. I do not have a local Windows build of R, so
the patch has been tested only by the Windows builds there.
